system_overview: This specification models Safra's algorithm for distributed termination detection on a ring, published as EWD 998: 'Shmuel Safra's version of termination detection'. The algorithm extends Dijkstra's EWD 840 to support asynchronous message delivery between nodes while still assuming reliable message channels and non-faulty nodes. Each node maintains a counter tracking the difference between sent and received messages, and the circulating token accumulates these counters to determine whether all messages have been delivered.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring (numbered 0 through N-1) and a circulating token. The system is divided into two subsystems: System (the termination detection algorithm controlling token passing and probe initiation) and Environment (the underlying computation with message sending, receiving, and node deactivation). The token carries a position, an accumulated message counter, and a color.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) activation status of each node (active or inactive), (2) color of each node (white or black), (3) a counter for each node representing the difference between messages sent and received by that node, (4) the number of pending (in-transit) messages at each node, and (5) a token record containing its current position, accumulated counter value, and color.
initial_state: Node activation and colors may take any type-correct values. All per-node counters are initialized to zero. No messages are pending. The token may be at any node, has a counter of zero, and is colored black.
actions: The algorithm defines the following actions: (1) Initiate probe: when the token is at node 0 and the previous round was inconclusive (token is black, node 0 is black, or the accumulated counter plus node 0's counter is positive), node 0 sends a fresh white token with counter zero to node N-1, painting itself white. (2) Pass token: an inactive node holding the token passes it to the next lower-numbered node, adding its counter to the token's counter and staining the token black if the node is black, then painting itself white. (3) Send message: an active node increments its counter and nondeterministically places a pending message at another node. (4) Receive message: a node with pending messages decrements its counter, paints itself black, and becomes active. (5) Deactivate: an active node becomes inactive.
safety_properties: Termination detection is sound: when the token is at node 0, the token is white, the token's counter plus node 0's counter equals zero, node 0 is white, and node 0 is inactive, then all nodes are inactive and no messages are in flight. Safra's inductive invariant ensures this through five disjuncts involving the relationship between the token position, node counters, pending messages, node colors, and the token color.
liveness_properties: If the computation terminates (all nodes inactive and no messages in flight), then termination is eventually detected.
model_bounds: The number of nodes N is a constant positive natural number. A state constraint limits each node's counter to at most 3, each node's pending messages to at most 3, and the token's counter to at most 9.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for the System actions (token passing and probe initiation). Message channels are reliable (no message loss). Nodes do not fail. The specification refines the abstract AsyncTerminationDetection specification through a refinement mapping. The algorithm is correct for arbitrary ring sizes.
